slides.title: 4.1: Text Generation (The Wordsmiths)
content: Most common type of AI.
Powered by Large Language Models (LLMs).
Understand and generate human language.
slides.narration:
Let's explore text generation.
This is very common.
It uses Large Language Models, or LLMs.
LLMs understand human language.
They also generate it fluently.
slides.image_prompt: Graphic showing a large brain-like icon representing an LLM, with text flowing in as input and text flowing out as output. Gears turning inside the brain.

slides.title: What They're Used For:
content: Many real-world applications.

They have many real-world uses.

slides.title: Key Applications
content: Summarization: Condense long texts.
Translation: Convert between languages.
slides.narration:
First, consider summarization.
It condenses long texts.
Then, consider translation.
It converts languages quickly.
See the power?
slides.image_prompt: Two distinct icons: one showing a long document shrinking into a short bulleted list, and another showing two speech bubbles with different language symbols (e.g., 'A' and '語').

slides.title: Understanding AI Hallucinations
content: AI models predict the next token, not 'know' facts.
They generate plausible but incorrect statements.
This is a significant risk for users.
slides.narration:
Now let's discuss AI hallucinations.
This is a critical topic in Generative AI.
AI models predict the next token.
They select the most probable one.
This process does not involve consciousness.
AI doesn't have knowledge or intention.
It cannot distinguish between facts and fiction.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon illustration of a confused robot generating text bubbles with nonsensical or factually incorrect information mixed with plausible-looking text. Question marks surrounding the robot's head.

slides.title: Mitigating Hallucinations
content: Fact-checking is crucial for AI output.
Verify information with reliable sources.
Use AI as a tool, not an authority.
slides.narration:
How do we mitigate these issues?
Fact-checking is crucial for AI output.
Always verify information with reliable sources.
Treat AI as a powerful tool.
It is not an ultimate authority.
slides.image_prompt: A person using a magnifying glass to inspect text from an AI chatbot on a screen. A checkmark and a cross mark are near the text. Reliable source icons are in the background.

slides.title: Prompt Engineering (Advanced)
content: Refine prompts for better accuracy.
Provide context or examples.
Example: 'Summarize this article, ensuring all facts are cited from the text.'
Example: 'Translate this paragraph, then list any ambiguous phrases.'
slides.narration:
For advanced users, consider prompt engineering.
Refine your prompts for better accuracy.
Provide context or specific examples to the AI.
For instance, ask it to cite facts.
You can also list ambiguous phrases after translation.
This guides the AI more effectively.
slides.image_prompt: A person typing a detailed, structured prompt into an AI interface. The interface shows examples of good prompts. Gears are turning, representing refinement.

slides.title: Recap and Assignment
content: Text generation uses LLMs for many tasks.
Applications include summarization, translation, chatbots, content creation, sentiment analysis.
AI hallucinations are plausible but incorrect statements.
Always fact-check critical information from LLMs.
Your Assignment: Use an LLM, summarize an article, ask a niche question, and fact-check results.
slides.narration:

Its applications include summarization and translation.
